newsitem.title: USA: Latin debt prices slip as investors watch and wait.
newsitem.headline: Latin debt prices slip as investors watch and wait.

text.p: Latin American debt prices slipped Thursday as U.S. investors stayed out of the market and left dealers to bid prices lower, traders said.
"It is a fairly confusing moment," said the head Brady bond trader of a large U.S. investment house. "I don't think there are a lot of investors who want to commit money one way or the other."
The flow of trade slowed from Wednesday's frenetic pace, as players saw little to inspire them.
"What we are going through is a buyers strike," one Brady trader said. "People have cash but they are not spending it."
The trader said that only around 15 percent of his firm's activity was conducted with customers and the remainder with other trading houses, compared with a typical 50-50 split.
"I think a lot of people are fairly neutral so positions in the street should not be particularly large," another large trader said.

"What we are seeing is a lot less risk apppetite in the region and a lot lower volumes," said Walter Molano, Latin American economist at SBC Warburg. "In this type of market an investor has to be very careful."
Argentine FRBs dropped 3/4 to a bid price of 79-3/4, and Brazilian Cs gave up 7/8 to 68-3/4.
"The guys who were caught long don't really have the wherewithal or the willingness to go longer," one Brady trader said. "Until the buyers come out it's very easy to push the market down."
